query: The Revision Tables The librarians have set out the revision tables early this term: past papers, model answers, and a sign promising the lamps stay lit until the bell. {~Footnote is asleep on last year's Evocation paper.|A shelf has rearranged itself into exam order, which it has never done for anyone before.|Someone has left a full set of notes behind, with a note of their own: "Take them. I passed."} Sit down and revise {~You work through two past papers and most of a third. The questions start to look like ones you have seen before, which is the point.|You copy out the model answers until your hand aches, then close the book and write them again from memory. Mostly right.|By the bell you have a page of everything you didn't know this morning. It is a shorter page than you feared.} Not today {~You leave the tables to the people who look more worried than you. The afternoon is yours.|You borrow a novel instead and read it in the window seat. The exams can wait for another day, you hope.|You nod at the revision tables on your way past, like an acquaintance you mean to call on.} Take notes with the owl quill {~The owl quill takes your notes tidier than your hand could, and then underlines the bits you'll be asked. You argue with it for an hour.|The quill writes faster than you think. By the bell you have a page of everything, in a hand you could almost be proud of.|You let the quill copy out the model answers. It corrects your spelling, then your reasoning, then your posture.}
